This study analyzes the highest-energy cosmic ray component ($E/ \text{EeV} > 8$), utilizing data from the Pierre Auger Observatory. An examination of the angular distribution of cosmic rays with energies exceeding 8 Exaelectronvolts reveals a pronounced alteration in the modulation pattern. This shift, observed at the requested threshold, involves a change in the pattern's shape. Furthermore, the energy at which modulation occurs has been identified as having been reduced by approximately 10%. These findings hold significant value for refining our comprehension of ultra-high-energy processes.

This study presents the initial experimental results concerning fluctuations in the transverse momentum-dependent flow angle, $v_n$, and magnitude, $v_n$, derived from newly developed four-particle correlators. Data collected via ALICE in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV, show that such fluctuations occur across a spectrum of centralities, peaking in the most central collisions for transverse p T > 2 GeV/c. Model comparisons using iEBE-VISHNU and UrQMD indicate these observations primarily reflect the early stages of the heavy-ion interaction, with late-stage fluctuations included only as minor contributions. The observed fluctuations in the flow angle exceed previously predicted values, challenging current theoretical frameworks that struggle to reconcile these findings with their descriptions of macroscopic viscosity, thermal fluctuations, and pressure gradient variance. Furthermore, these findings cannot be accounted for merely by adjusting standard global parameters to accommodate initial conditions characterized by strong temperature and density gradients.

This study examines the challenges of managing discrepancies in relational tables containing missing values (nulls) alongside functional dependencies (FDs). While the conventional wisdom holds that table instances must adhere strictly to all imposed FDs, it is crucial to develop methodologies addressing how instances that violate some dependencies can be managed concerning nulls, specifically by developing methods for defining and assessing consistency with respect to FD constraints that incorporate the concept of uniqueness rectangle. This paper introduces several foundational contributions in relational database theory, namely: (1) a catalog of diverse inconsistency scenarios arising when dealing with tables populated by unknown entries; (2) corresponding consistency models designed for handling these unknowns under functional dependency regimes; (3) an exploration of how such unknown entries influence various standard data quality indicators; (2) an analysis of the computational complexities associated with determining consistency for different tables; and (3) an investigation into table instances where consistency is satisfied by a specific set of FD constraints containing unknowns, referred to as (FD, ?)-tables. In scenarios involving tables with unknowns that satisfy specific FD constraints, this paper has offered insightful results relevant to areas such as data cleaning, data mining, and relation schema analysis.

Achieving this target relies on wide-field photometry spanning diverse altitudes, which speeds up VAOD derivation without needing the system's absolute calibration, while simultaneously delivering that calibration incidentally. By combining several years of FRAM (F/Φ)otometric Robotic Atmospheric Monitor telemetry from Argentina at the 1.3-metre UTRC-ESPRIT telescope with South African data from the 0.6-metre FRAM instrument at the STAR-2 facility, the authors observe that their skyVEOM (Vertical Aerosol Optical Depth) technique typically yields 0.015 VAOD per hour, with South African observations achieving 0.010 VAOD in just thirty minutes. Object pose estimation has long been a critical and extensively researched topic in computer vision. In this survey, we organize the related literature into two major groups: deep learning-free approaches and deep learning-driven approaches, and cover relevant studies within each subgroup. While both categories have seen profound advancement and progress, we believe this organized review will prove beneficial to researchers and practitioners navigating the evolving field. As we conclude, we identify current limitations and emerging challenges, as well as prospective directions for future research.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to solve general graph-structured sparse covariance estimation problems. This approach integrates prior knowledge about covariance structures, potentially reflecting physical or thermodynamic systems, alongside automatic learning of remaining structure sparsity, thereby facilitating high-dimensional systems where the variable count exceeds sample counts. GGLasso supports diverse constraints on graph class, directed as well as undirected graphs, and efficiently handles both convex and concave divergence risks. The package includes utilities for handling directed graphs and estimating precision matrices under joint convex-divisible risk functions, positioned as specific extensions beyond the original GELASSO framework. In terms of performance metrics and asymptotic analysis for these extended cases, we establish convergence rate guarantees. Furthermore, we adapt the algorithm for group-oriented sparse covariance matrices and assess its performance across various synthetic scenarios.

This study examines Umbrella Sampling (US) and Harmonic Biasing (HB) potentials within the context of protein dynamics simulated via Molecular Dynamics (MD). We analytically derive the configurational averages arising from both approaches and introduce an innovative, unbiased MD weighting protocol. In this new setup, systems governed by US and harmonic biasing schemes run in parallel, each yielding well-weighted configurational averages that require significantly reduced sampling, alongside a basic unweighted simulation. Integrating results from these three distinct simulations guarantees accurate unbiased configurational averages. Applied to the folding of the Trp-cage miniprotein, our methodology reveals that achieving accurate biases from harmonic-bounded Umbrella Sampling (specifically updating spring constants every 50 MD steps) requires approximately a tenfold reduction in MD timescales compared to standard U.S. stiffness parameters of 1 nm. Notably, harmonic biasing provides superior accuracy relative to US even when applied as the primary uncorrected approach. Ultimately, this low-cost weighted scheme ensures accurate uncorrected results.

We introduce a novel method for computing a specific type of eigenvector centrality applicable to multilayer networks subject to cross-layer constraints on node significance. These networks consist of multiple layers—each an edge-weighted and potentially directed graph sharing the same set of nodes—but lack direct inter-layer connections. Similar to classic eigenvector centrality, a node's importance within a layer depends on the weighted relevance of its neighbors within that same layer. However, unlike the standard model, we allow both the adjacency relations and the importance values to be influenced by different layers. Crucially, existing multilayer centrality frameworks utilizing explicit inter-layer dependencies only partially support such constrained, layer-specific requirements. In our proposed model, these constraints define centrality scores through a combination of independent eigenvalue problems and dependent pseudo-eigenvalue problems, which can be solved efficiently via an interleaved power iteration approach.

Subsequently, by applying a specific covariantization to both this space and the groupoid, we transform them into constant de Sitter time and the Hagen-Sommer Rotor groupoid, respectively. These outcomes confirm the equivalence between the two pseudo-linear models and demonstrate they describe opposite signs of de Sitter spacetime curvature.

We investigate the spectral properties of a low-symmetry 2D electronic lattice: a herringbone system within a non-symmorphic wallpaper group defined by orthogonal glide symmetries along two sets of directions. Using a nearest-neighbour tight-binding framework incorporating horizontal and vertical hopping, we identify two inequivalent Dirac cones located along a specific path in the first Brillouin zone (FBZ). Due to the presence of two inequivalent points on the same high-symmetry FBZ edge, the real-space unit cell is effectively doubled relative to the simple herringbone structure. Both the expanded real-space and reciprocal-space Brillouin zones are displayed, and the evolution of Dirac points across all symmetry-equivalent paths in the full FBZ is depicted in a band structure. We analyze the inversion symmetry relations of the Dirac cones relative to the central high-symmetry point (G-point) and determine their tangible formation origins. Specifically, one group of Dirac points arises from hopping patterns between sub-lattices that align with orthogonal glides in the herringbone layout; these disappear if hopping is disabled between adjacent sites sharing an orthogonal glide relationship. The second group stems from hopping between two inequivalent atomic positions along a diagonal. Finally, we outline how an experimental two-dimensional herringbone crystal could induce similar Dirac points, suggesting that such features likely exist in multiple low-symmetry 2F-lated materials.

We produce Single-Photon Catalyzed Coherent States (SPCCSs) utilizing quantum optical methods that depend either on beam splitters (BS) or parametric amplifiers (PA). To obtain these states, a coherent state and a single-photon Fock state at two input ports undergo interaction with the device; simultaneously, detecting one photon in the second output port yields the desired state. We demonstrate that SPCCS generation via a beam splitter results from the absence of photon number exchange between modes, whereas using a parametric amplifier arises from the cancellation of photon addition and subtraction operations. The quantum characteristics of SPCCSs produced via both techniques are thoroughly analyzed, including quantum fluctuations, photon statistics, quantum non-classicality, and single-photon procurement probabilities. Comparisons are provided between the outcomes of beam splitter and parametric amplifier implementations to evaluate their respective properties.

The application of bivectors within General Relativity and the Newman-Penrose formalism is essential for formulating the exact solutions of Einstein's field equations. This paper serves as a guided introduction to the core principles of GR and specific implementations via the Newman-Penrose framework, with a concentrated focus on defining and characterizing gravitational bivectors. It aims to lay the necessary groundwork for subsequent studies that employ this concept within a revised (rationalized) Newman-Penrose formalism to solve Einstein's field equations in the context of diverse physical scenarios.

Delineating esophageal tumors in CT scans presents a dual challenge for manual and automatic segmentation: the low tissue contrast near the malignancies and the organ's complex, variable anatomy. While automated methods have improved, they frequently depend on extensive structure-from-motion (SfM) data sets for training, and neither approach fully mitigates the inherent difficulties. This work introduces a fully automatic segmentation pipeline that integrates an intensity-only convolutional neural network (CNN) with a novel fully automatic organ localization technique based on fully connected stochastic networks (FCSN). The method proceeds in two phases: first, the organ boundaries are estimated by locating the lung gastro-frenial angle (LFGA)—the junction where the esophagus connects to the diaphragm—using an FCSN trained on this specific landmark; second, the organ contour is derived by expanding from the LFGA detection in one of three fully automatic directions. The pipeline was evaluated using data from 170 patients containing labeled tumor and healthy tissue segments. Subsequently, the methodology's efficacy for facilitating both automatic segmentation and manual contouring was assessed on a cohort of 280 additional clinical scans that lacked ground truth annotations.

Defined as advanced capability in two or more languages for both spoken and written communication, multilingualism frequently manifests through code-switching or code-mixing within individual sentences. This work reviews existing natural language processing (NLP) literature regarding its limitations and obstacles when addressing five critical social impact areas: crisis response, healthcare support, political engagement, anti-disinformation initiatives, and hate speech mitigation in multilingual communities. Furthermore, we introduce prospective datasets, models, and utilities poised to propel multilingual NLP research toward broader societal benefits. Utilizing English-Hindi mixing as a case study allows for representative inferences applicable to other languages pairs.

Automatic image description models are typically built and assessed using the GEM dataset, with new methodologies frequently ranked against existing baseline methods. However, since most studies rely on simple metrics like BERTScore to evaluate these descriptions, they fail to reflect actual human utility or accuracy. To address this gap, we introduce diverse, task-oriented evaluation approaches for image captions, including utilization by visual question answering (VQA) models, human judges, and detection networks such as SBERT and others. Results on the test set demonstrate significant improvements across all introduced scoring methods when compared to standard baseline evaluations.

This combined approach accurately captures both metallic and covalent bonding behaviors. Our findings indicate that phonon structures and specific heat capacities vary significantly with temperature. Furthermore, REBO-AEP yields more accurate specific heat predictions compared to standalone REBO. Based on these results, Ta$_2$O$_5$ melts approximately at 3100 K,321 based on its complex crystalline structure and strong covalent bonds. The precise data obtained from this study will assist in selecting the laser parameters needed for tantalum oxide film fabrication via pulse laser deposition.

Conversational interfaces, which utilize natural language interfaces like voice and text to facilitate human-computer interaction, have gained immense popularity. Research into these technologies addresses numerous domains, including human-computer dialogue management, dialogue state assessment, and natural language generation. Among these, machine comprehension stands out as a crucial subfield of natural language processing, enabling systems to generate informed and contextually relevant responses by integrating prior knowledge. In specific, this paper introduces a novel framework, Babel, designed for assessing understanding within human conversation by transforming the task into a question-answalling setup. Babel extracts assessable content from dialogue while filtering out uncontrollable or redundant information, and employs an extended version of the SQuAD dataset to formulate query-based assessments. Evaluations indicate that Babel offers a robust and practical methodology for measuring linguistic competence in conversational systems.

Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) has gained significant interest from researchers for its potential to mitigate data sparsity in recommender systems. Nevertheless, existing single- or dual-target CDR techniques frequently encounter specific limitations. First, they often rely on a single target domain, which can lead to the accumulation of noise and biased data. Second, traditional methods typically assume full domain adaptation, ignoring the high translation costs associated with different domain characteristics. Addressing these challenges, we introduce MSDCR, a novel Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation framework. This innovative approach utilizes implicit feedback to suggest sparsely data domains while simultaneously enhancing user profiles across other domains. Specifically, MSDCR leverages user behavior in input domain to enrich user representations in one or more target domains, ultimately enabling recommendation in additional sparse environments. Furthermore, MSDCR employs a multi-task learning architecture that facilitates the transfer of implicit feedback from other sources. To ensure the model's effectiveness, extensive experiments were conducted on three real-world datasets, confirming that MSDCR significantly outperforms current baseline techniques in terms of recommendation accuracy.

Although prior research has demonstrated that exponential numbers of linear and quadratic equidimentional equations can be expressed using sums of squares (SOS) in polynomials—and thus as distances between squares-of-norms—there remains a scarcity of work extending this approach to general cone formulations. This paper addresses that void by presenting an Efficient Cones Optimization Procedure (ECO) method capable solving ACOPs featuring finite but exponentially large numbers of linear and quadratic monomial equalities. Additionally, exponential counts of exotic-cone constraints can be condensed far more generally than previously achievable with simpler models, enabling the immediate resolution of ACOPs defined by both sums and products. Rapidly advancing automated quality control (QC) methods are causing false rejections of acceptable images, which is why integrating automated systems with human review is essential. This study evaluates an AI-driven QC framework designed to prioritize the reliability and efficiency of MRI analysis. Key features included are a decision-support score, visual explanations, and a customizable interface that organizes samples by severity. Established on the large MRIQC 1.0 training set, this framework was tested using both a population of roughly 1000 images and an algorithmically generated population of 10,000,000 images (the "ImageNomad"). When evaluated against the original dataset's ground truth, a threshold of 0.29 on the decision score effectively separated rejectable images from retainable ones. Separating a human expert assessment of the Nomad dataset yielded a correlation of 0.833, demonstrating that the system reliably mirrors human judgments in this large-scale environment. The Nomand tool offers an adaptable, transparent, and highly effective QC utility suitable for adoption across diverse clinical environments.

This paper examines the impact of privately owned electric vehicles on power system stability during disruptions. To capture the decentralized interactions within transportation and energy domains, we introduce a Network-based Multi-Agent Optimization (N-MAO) framework formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP). Leveraging network-flow theories and multi-agent principles, this model represents both vehicle mobility choices and load management strategies, notably integrating a v2g (vehicle-to-grid) framework constrained by realistic V2G operational dynamics such as driver travel schedules and electricity tariff rates. To solve this optimization problem, we develop an effective branch-and-price algorithm enhanced with specialized pricing problems and cutting planes. Numerical simulations evaluate the practicality of the suggested model and optimization algorithm across standard and disruption-injected test systems featuring various vehicle penetration rates.

Autonomous mobile agents are increasingly vital and will likely handle many daily tasks for us in the near future. These agents must navigate while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles; while standard path-planning algorithms handle this well, they typically overlook the self-loops common in everyday movements. To address this, we introduced "Motivation Dynamics," a framework that manages both navigation and self-looping behaviors autonomously. By combining a motivational driver with dynamic system theory, the system enables agents to learn how to achieve specific goals and form self-loops during the training phase. Furthermore, the framework supports flexibility in adapting to newly learned goals or loops. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments confirm the effectiveness of this approach.

This study investigates the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and the solid solution Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ ($x$ = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0). The full-electron augmented-plane-wave method was employed to model their crystal structures and electronic properties. Both pure compounds and the intermediate phases adopt the AuCu$_3$-type lattice structure (space group Pm-3m). Calculations reveal that both GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ possess predominantly non-metallic features. Additionally, spin magnetic moments were evaluated for both materials. Unlike the individual elements, no phase separates during the formation of the solid solution; rather, it forms a continuous series exhibiting V-shaped magnetization behavior typical of atomic dilution solutions. A distinct inflection point in the V-shape emerges at the stoichiometric composition of the Gd and Cm tin intermetallic compound. The study attributes this phenomenon to two competing mechanisms: the formation of the AuCu$_3$-type crystal phase and the substitution of Cm for Gd. Ultimately, theoretical predictions align well with available experimental data.

We examine predictions within the bilepton model, an extension of the standard model that modifies the gauge group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3) \times U(1)$. This alteration necessitates that fermions in the fundamental representation be organized into color triplets, implying the existence of new charged lepton partners. Such partners could potentially resolve the opening issue of the muon. Furthermore, this model predicts scalar bileptons capable of mediating same-sign dilepton signals in both initial and large final states while circumventing certain experimental constraints. Consequently, it offers a compelling framework for future high-energy colliders, notably the 1000 Tep future hadron collider.

The Orbit Generating Systems (OGS) for non-abelian groups offer a meaningful extension of the canonical basis found in finite abelian groups. An OGS is characterized by the unique representation of each group element as a specific, ordered product of powers of designated generators. While R. Genomic annotations are increasingly utilized to clarify genetic associations made through genome-wide association studies (GWAS); however, the predictive accuracy of many such annotations often trails that of genomic sequence alone. We examined extensive GWAS catalogs to identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) linked to human traits, paying specific attention to DNase-I sensitivity and DNase-I cleavage fragment frequency. Utilizing four distinct metrics derived from DNase-I assays, we demonstrate that a significant overrepresentation of SNPs resides within DNase-I hypersensitive sites (DHSs), an effect that persists strongly even after accounting for DHS fragment frequency. Furthermore, we analyzed the DNase-I cleavage profiles of regions containing these SNPs and discovered a marked accumulation of variants within DHSs exhibiting high local cleavage activity. Finally, we synthesized this DNase-I based insight with other genomic annotations linked to SNPs. The resulting integrated framework significantly enhances the explanation power for GWAS findings across diverse trait categories, including blood cellular composition, blood-related characteristics, immune system functions, cancer susceptibility, as well as physiological and behavioral traits influenced during development and early life.

Developing numerical schemes for time-dependent partial differential equations often requires them to maintain essential features of the continuous solution, such as conservation laws or other geometric attributes. A substantial legacy exists in the study of discretization schemes that preserve such structures, encompassing both theoretical validations of standard methods and innovative designs offering both high-order precision and exact preservation. However, when integrated with implicit tanning steps, these methods carry a significant drawback: maintaining structure preservation typically demands the exact solution of the discrete system at each time-step. While this constraint is manageable for small systems, it becomes infeasible for the extensive linear systems generated by standard spatial-temporal PDE discretization for larger scales. This paper introduces a modification to the flexible generalized minimum residual (FGMRES) algorithm that imposes specific constraints on approximate solutions. The proposed approach is applied to both parabolic and hyperbolic conservation laws to demonstrate its utility, demonstrating both high-order consistency and the generation of highly accurate conserved results.

Non-rigid registration stands as a fundamental technique in soft-tissue navigation, specifically within laparoscopic liver surgery. Our work addresses the challenge of mapping a preoperative CT-derived organ model onto the intraoperative surface of the liver, reconstructed from surgical camera feeds. The core of our approach lies in a two-stage surface feature correspondence system. Initially, a correspondence framework establishes alignment between the preoperative and intraoperative surfaces by integrating non-rigid registration with shape-based matching. Subsequently, a new method establishes feature-level alignment between the live and virtual textures. This feature correspondence tool is designed to assist navigators in navigating along the surface of the actual organ. Furthermore, this methodology allows surgeons to instantly access and apply knowledge about the individual patient's anatomy and specific pathological traits gained prior to surgery. Finally, we provide a theoretical framework and evaluation metrics for quantifying the quality of these correspondences and the resulting spatial transformations. This paper presents a new surface-based navigation aid for liver surgery, combining virtual and real-time data to enhance safety and efficacy by establishing accurate anatomical links.

Scene flow involves predicting three-dimensional motion vectors for specific points within a dynamic three-dimensional environment. While these motion vectors provide significant advantages for subsequent tasks like detecting action types or avoiding collisions, obtaining them via LiDAR or stereo cameras demands significant computational resources and manual labor for precise labeling. To mitigate these annotation obstacles, we offer two solutions.

First, we created a 3D scene flow benchmark featuring datasets tailored to analyze the complexities of flow prediction in one hand. This involves training and evaluating models on data ranging from static to highly dynamic settings with varying depth and motion diversity, and also conducting analysis of errors and evaluating model performance.

Second, we introduced a model designed to anticipate 3D motion by processing vertical strips of a point cloud, with one hand. This approach leverages the spatial distribution and intrinsic geometry to manage most movements while effectively processing more difficult cases like rotation and it can operate in real time on a standard GPU.

Together, these initiatives advance our understanding and application of 3D motion estimation.

Radiation constraints inherent to positron emission tomography (PET) imaging hinder its application for studying vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, children, adults needing frequent scans, and potential risk applicants. Furthermore, our analysis examines which entities neural solvers designate as primary discourse centers, finding strong agreement between these selections and centering predictions. Evaluations across three distinct tasks demonstrate that models fine-tuned on data generated by our method achieve superior performance compared to those trained on other methods, with the benefit clearly due in part to effective utilization of real instances.

Accurately and quickly predicting river flow velocities is critical for various applications, such as managing flood risks and optimizing hydroelectric generation. Although traditional numerical solvers achieve high precision, their slow runtimes often hinder real-time use. Additionally, the complexity of flow dynamics makes selecting a precise turbulence closure model challenging. To address these issues, we introduce a data-driven approach based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting both laminar and turbulent velocity fields in two-dimensional channel flows with an unknown free-surface tension coefficient. Our findings demonstrate that training on simulated data enables this ML framework to outperform other ML methods by accurately reconstructing detailed spatial velocity profiles—something traditional Integral Models and $k-\omega$ SST models struggle to match—while also significantly reducing computation time compared to standard solvers. However, the study notes a key constraint: the model's dependence on Reynolds number, suggesting that expanding the training dataset across diverse physical and geometric scenarios could further enhance the robustness of this ML solution.

High-dynamic-range (HDR) imaging is achieved by merging a set of exposures taken at varying levels, allowing devices like smartphones with limited internal dynamic ranges to capture full brightness and contrast. Comparative analyses against existing benchmarks confirm the method's efficiency and computational effectiveness.

Causal deep learning represents a significant and emerging subfield of machine learning focused on developing structured, interpretable models capable of robust predictions. By imposing specific constraints on network architecture and utilizing advanced regularization techniques, this approach facilitates reliable inference even during distributional drift. By integrating domain knowledge with theoretical frameworks, these models effectively isolate the most informative causal features for forecasting. Furthermore, they enable researchers to map out complex interfeature relationships, identify novel causal components, and uncover the underlying generative processes of the data.

This note introduces and analyzes a new class of maps known as oriented colored broken submersions. It represents the most fundamental class of maps complying with an h-principle (here referred to as b-principle); in two dimensions, it approximates oriented submersions notably by ensuring every oriented colored broken submersion from a 2-manifold to a closed, simply-connected manifold is boardant to a submersion. Additionally, we demonstrate that the Madsen-Weiss theorem (the well-known Mumford Conjecture), fits effectively this overarching b-principle framework. Given an h-version of the principle applicable to these maps alongside Harer stability and Miller Morita results, a derivation of the Madsen-Weiss (Munford) theorem becomes viable.

This study presents a performance evaluation comparing CHEbychev and ILU($k$) preconditioners for solving cardiac mechanics equations using the FEM-discretized momentum balance and Stokes equations. Within a performance framework, we examined computational cost, convergence metrics, and solution accuracy. We highlighted the influence of mesh topology and mesh physics on chemieq performance, noting that although both methods exhibit grid-dependent convergence based on the condition number—which scales with elements' condition number—CHEbychev performance degrades significantly for complex geometries as the condition number increases. Furthermore, we demonstrated that mesh element orientation significantly influences both chemieq and ILB's convergence rates. Regarding cost metrics, we found a per-iteration expense disparity of approximately two to three orders of magnitude between the two, favoring ILB. While chemieq generally converges faster in iterations, ILB's overall efficiency, lower per-step cost, and robustness make it the optimal choice for simulating cardiac mechanics across various mesh types and physical models, with the exception of transmembrane action potential solving where a highly constrained 0.0001 relative tolerance nullifies its benefits. We finalizing with a framework integrating relative and absolute tolerances to mitigate numerical issues arising from ILB's fixed-point iteration.

Standard diffusive expansion is typified by a Gaussian distribution where the mean square displacement scales linearly against time, yet this standard behavior fails when correlations or heterogeneity arise. Consequently, this study analyzes the diffusion of fractional (long-time memory-corrupted), Brownian walkers under conditions of varying and spatially non-uniform diffusivity. The primary goal involves translating these microscopic, individual attributes visible as population-scale temporal evolution into physical insights regarding the broader context of self-similar diffusion. Furthermore, the work evaluates the viability of linking such features across various self-similar diffusion regimes, detailing both the potential and inherent constraints. Results are structured within a unified framework applied here to classic phenomena, including linear and nonlinear Laplace diffusive systems, along with their respective variations.

We have established a theoretical model designed to pinpoint the onset of linear coupling, scattering, and Kerr nonlinearity within a pair of interacting optical resonators of arbitrary geometry. The resulting framework identifies four distinct categories of nonlinear phenomena based on whether the system is or isn't in a phase where mode degeneracy exists, alongside the nature of that degeneracy. The study examines both theoretical cases and experimental setups featuring a nonlinear microdisk and a nonlinear microsphere interacting via scattering. We investigate how these systems can yield either coherent resonance crossing or an abrupt transition, depending on whether a degenerate mode remains undamped. Furthermore, we detail the conditions required to generate a large-area coherent resonance coupling (often referred to as coherent resonance coupling) and contrast this with the abrupt shift in transmission that occurs without full coupling. Finally, the paper outlines a method for quantifying the threshold of nonlinearity needed to trigger the sudden transmission switch in general configurations.

This study introduces a deep learning framework that utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to recover high-resolution turbulent velocity fields from very low-resolution data across various Reynolds numbers. The Multiscale Enhanced Super-Resolution GAN (MS-ESRGAN) serves as the model for reconstruction and is assessed using direct numerical simulation (DNS) of turbulent channel flows with large longitudinal ribs tested at multiple Reynolds numbers. The findings indicate the model's capability to accurately generate high-resolution velocity fields, encompassing both field properties and turbulent statistics, from inputs derived from two distinct low-resolution resolutions. Furthermore, the results demonstrate the model's potential for supergeneralization by reconstructing velocity fields at Reynolds levels different from those used during training, without additional instruction or adaptation for those specific cases, effectively handling unseen scenarios in its scope.

Although significant advancements have been made in applying reinforcement learning to robotics, gaming, and other demanding areas, considerable obstacles persist when deploying these algorithms in critical, evolving open-world settings. A primary issue remains the tendency of reinforcement learning models to generalize poorly to new tasks lying outside their training data distributions; consequently, continuous addition of training data is often necessary to handle new activities. Furthermore, integrating complex real-world elements—such as autonomous navigation and diverse hardware—renders troubleshooting extremely difficult. To address these challenges, we introduce OpenWORLD RL, an platform enabling streamlined experimentation and effective debugging of reinforcement learning algorithms on substantial open-world tasks. This system integrates a closed-loop translation workflow allowing researchers to write task logic in high-level programming languages and compile it directly into trainable RL environments. We also develop automated systems for real-time logging, visualization, and validation of environment states and agent actions. Equipped with this infrastructure, researchers can rapidly prototype tasks by injecting real-world data and refine task definitions to detect and address generalization failures or environmental bugs. To demonstrate its utility, we implemented an air-traffic-control task using two distinct real-world robotics platforms. In this application, drones navigate an open world to safely pick up and deliver packages while avoiding collisions, operating within a trained distribution without requiring RL-specific hardware simplifications. Finally, the task was mastered using two different algorithms: one trained in simulation with transfer learning and another trained entirely in the open world with real-world feedback.

By representing this classification task as a state in a diagram, the method effectively identifies each process with its corresponding structural model. This method was tested on real-world payment data from the "chameleon" project and will compare the outcomes against current state-of-the-art methodologies.

Feature extraction offers a viable strategy to mitigate dimensionality challenges within high-dimensional datasets. As a prevalent self-supervised learning technique, contrastive learning has recently attracted substantial interest. In this research, we introduced a unified framework grounded in a novel interpretation of contrastive learning, applicable to both unsupervised and supervised feature extraction tasks. The framework first establishes two contrastive (CL) graphs to distinctly identify positive and negative pairs; subsequently, the projection matrix is obtained by minimizing the corresponding contrastive loss function to integrate information from both similar and dissimilar examples for unifying unsupervised and supervised extraction processes. Specifically, we detail three methodologies: one unsupervised CL approach, along with two supervised CL variants. Extensive numerical tests across five real-world datasets highlight the framework's superior performance relative to state-of-the-art methods.

Model selection or sparse modelling for categorical variables remains problematic, even with a moderate variable count, as encoding each category requires a parameter, quickly leading to non-solutions. Although Group Lasso is an established and efficient tool for selecting continuous or categorical variables, its estimates for individual levels of selected factors are rarely identical. Because of the lack uniformity, resulting models often fail to achieve true sparsity, hindering interpretability. We address this by proposing a two-stage strategy: initially, dimensionality is reduced using Group Lasso; subsequently, final selection is made over a narrowed candidate space via an information criterion applied to clusters of factor levels constructed after the initial selection phase. We examine algorithm accuracy within sparse, high-dimensional contexts, applying our approach to both synthetic examples and realistic datasets, demonstrating that our methods generally outperform current-state-of-the-art algorithms regarding prediction accuracy or model size efficiency at the variable dimension.

Although Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit human-like capabilities across numerous natural language tasks, it has remained largely unexamined whether their performance benefits more from training on factual statements embedded in knowledge graphs (KGs) rather than conventional text. This study presents the pretraining of KG-aware LLMs directly from KGs and investigates if this method confers advantages over standard sentences for knowledge-related activities. We introduce Adapa, an adapter module designed to inject a knowledge-graph (KG) awareness into large language models without requiring extra supervisory data or fine-tuning. We also present results of a human-centric evaluation along with automated metrics on both ADapa's output quality and the accuracy of ADapa as an AI assistant working with large language models. Our findings show that an adapter-based model named ADapa, which was pretrained solely on KGs using the ADapa architecture, significantly boosts an基础 model's performance in KG-dependent tasks such as knowledge question answering, natural inference, and KG construction and query. We also analyze the sources and limits of these improvements through human tests and automated assessments to determine how well training on KGs compares to training on natural language sentences for equipping a model with encyclopedic knowledge. Our KG-pretrained model outperformed the baseline by 18.3% in KG-based question answering, 9.7% in natural inference, and 9.7% in KG-based question answering.

Spatial anti-aliasing is critical for both the visual quality and rendering performance of line joins where road segments intersect on vector maps. Given OpenGL's limitations, a standard approach involves splicing multiple triangles at various scales to approximate fan-shaped joins; however, this method introduces visual artifacts and suboptimal system performance. To address these issues, this paper introduces a streamlined and efficient algorithm that generates realistic fan-shaped curves with alpha blending using just two triangles derived from geometric computations, rather than multiple approximations. Experiments demonstrate that this technique offers a lifelike anti-aliasing result, lower memory consumption, higher frame rates, and efficient rendering without overlapping draws, making it well-suited for Internet mapping applications such as Tencent Maps and Baidu Maps.

We introduce a novel, extremely lightweight dual-Path Recurrent Neural Network (Dual-Path RNN, or DPRNN, for short), designed specifically for the separation of audio streams. This model design merges an exceptionally thin structure designed for detecting short-term patterns with a long short-term memory (LDM) module that handles extended timeframes. We call this configuration a dual structure because it addresses both temporal scales crucial for speech separation: very short and very long. Experiments show that having both time scales allows our dual structure to achieve strong performance on sequences much longer than those handled even by large dual structures. We believe this model could help extend the sequence lengths handled even by very large dual structures in actual audio stream separation applications.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models offer a dynamic alternative for enhancing the depiction of convection within weather and climate systems. Unlike traditional mass-flux convection schemes, this framework avoids assumptions invalid at current resolutions; however, it remains overly simplistic for weather models. This specific approach avoids excessive assumptions while proving suitable as a parameterization. Results presented utilize this two-fluid model in a state-variable based single-column model to simulate forced convection during the day and radiative cooling at night. Key features included are the formation of a nocturnal temperature inversion, the cyclic development and dissipation of convective activity from sunset to midnight, and cold clouds forming via radiative cooling. These results align well with observations, as do those generated using a basic 1979 Wyngaard and Cote two-fluid theory. This strong correspondence supports investigating other phenomena such as frontal processes and buoyancy-forces associated with marine stratocumulus systems under the experimental single-column setup employing a night-time fluid.

We examine three independent Jaynes-Cummings systems involving atom pairs where correlations exist between some atoms while the third remains initially uncorrelated. This non-trivial finding offers a potential method for generating multipartite-entangled atoms through Jaynes-Cummings interactions and could potentially be implemented using existing experimental setups.

Speech-emotion recognition (SER) empowers computers to interact emotionally intelligently. Although current SER models have achieved high accuracy on clean, studio-quality audio, accuracy drops significantly when deployed with live recordings containing noise and speaker variations. To address this, this paper presents a framework designed to amplify SER performance in real-time, noisy live audio streams by integrating time- and context-aware adaptations. Specifically, we introduce a dual dimension context (DDC) module that extracts contextual clues from both the passage of time and the surrounding linguistic environment to spawn dynamic new neural speakers (DNSNs)—synthetic models uniquely tailored to an individual's voice and speech habits. These focused neural networks enhance detection precision by isolating and reducing the impact of external distortions. Additionally, because most existing SR models output discrete emotion labels, we refine these outputs using additional context to generate more nuanced, hybrid outputs combining emotion types with confidence levels. Evaluations conducted on the REVAL dataset demonstrate the framework's effectiveness, yielding a 13.93% increase in F1 scores compared to standard baseline results.

Quenching and annealing represent opposing approaches to the time-evolution of quantum systems; annealing slowly adjusts a Hamiltonian's parameters to explore equilibrium phases for solving complex optimizations, while quenching imposes sudden changes that create non-equilibrium states. We examine the connection between both regimes, demonstrating that a dynamical quench parameter—determined by the distance between initial and final coupling settings—gently evolves to effectively restore annealing behavior. Although the mechanisms and diagnostic tools for these processes differ fundamentally, we identify their complementary natures, arguing that early-stage post-quench dynamics are governed by initial Hamiltonic couplings, whereas later-time evolution depends on the quench parameter. We highlight a key distinction: whereas annealing dynamics are driven by the inverse of the annealing schedule, quench dynamics follow a square-root temporal scaling, resulting in optimized annealing performance following a sudden initial phase. Furthermore, a fundamental incompatibility emerges between the minimal energy reached via an instantaneous quench and that achieved through annealing, implying that minimizing quantum annealing errors requires a final coupling strength significantly higher than the typical near-unity values typically selected. This inherent trade-off ensures that neither method can simultaneously achieve their theoretical theoretical limits, suggesting that adhering to a linear schedule reduces post-annealing fluctuations. However, adopting a specific non-linear time-dependent schedule can substantially lower average fluctuations, yielding improvement over the linear baseline.

"Beginning with an effective two-dimensional two-orbital model of infinite-layer nickelate, derived from $d$- and $s$-like orbitals, this study examines the validity of mapping the model onto a single-band Hubbard description. This paper introduces a novel approach to the containment problem for extended regular expressions, enhancing basic regex capabilities with intersection and complementation while handling infinite alphabets via potentially limitless character sets. Unlike traditional methods that fail to manage extended operators or such vast character collections, the proposed algorithm eliminates the necessity of converting expressions to equivalent automata. Instead, it utilizes a purely symbolic term rewriting system to resolve regular expression inequalities. Our method offers a new symbolic decision process grounded in derivatives of regex as defined by Brzozowski and the Antimirovian rewriting technique for containment checking. Specifically, we expand the standard Brzozowski syntactic derivative into derivative variants capable of operating across (potentially infinite) representable character sets.

Precise and resilient localization represents a critical requirement for autonomous mobile entities. Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) methods utilize data from cameras and inertial units to determine position and orientation, and recent deep learning approaches to VIO have garnered significant attention by delivering pose estimates through a data-driven paradigm, eliminating the need for manually designed heuristics. However, existing learning-based VIO models often exhibit suboptimal performance during training due to inaccuracies in ground-truth poses and localization labels, particularly in testing environments. To address this, we introduce a robust external visualization tracking loop for supervising the training of learning-based VIO. This loop provides a clean signal to ensure the maximization of localization learning signals during the process. Moreover, to further enhance the reliability of the training data, we develop an advanced data filtering mechanism based on optical flow. We embed this flow-based filter and tracking system into a comprehensive training loop, creating a loop that maximizes data quality and drives better model performance. This article examines a data completion problem for time-harmonic Maxwell equations regarding the electric field within a bounded domain. The goal involves reconstructing incomplete information from an impenetrable boundary segment using measurements obtained from an accessible part. The research investigates a non-iterative quasi-reversibility approach and introduces several alternative mixed variational formulations. Proofs are provided to establish the well-posedness, convergence, and regularity of the problem. Furthermore, after finite element discretization utilizing edge elements, diverse three- and two-dimensional numerical simulations demonstrate the method's efficacy, even when applied to data containing noise.

In this work, we investigate Federated Selective Aggregation (FedSA), an approach designed to train a student model for a specific new task using contributions from multiple decentralized teacher models with distinct and self-contained prior training. This study addresses a current challenge in model sharing, where significant investments are made toward creating robust networks that cannot be distributed due to concerns regarding privacy, security, or intellectual rights. While existing federated methods may help, our proposal goes further by enabling the student to specialize entirely differently than its source teacher models. To address this, we develop an agent-driven strategy where a unique saliency mechanism adaptatively identifies which teachers should be selected to inject specific capabilities. Evaluations in both single and multi-task environments demonstrate that FedSA successfully merges insights from these fragmented resources to deliver superior generalization and effectively handle one or more secondary tasks, a capability not supported by comparable methods.

Superconducting quantum circuits are recognized as a foremost platform in quantum computing. Achieving widespread practical viability within this field requires the identification and correction of material flaws that cause decoherence. This research employs terahertz spectroscopy to analyze the dielectric characteristics of aluminum films deposited on silicon, a widely used substrate for superconducting quantum processors. By applying a novel, non-parametric theoretical method to extract physical information from the resulting data, the study offers refined insights into the electrode-related sources of loss. According to these findings, surface oxides are responsible for approximately thirty percent of total losses at lower terahertz frequencies, while trapped surface states account for another twenty percent; both values represent three- to fourfold increases over previously reported figures. Consequently, engineering surfaces with diminished trapped states is posited as crucial for future quantum circuit designs to reach even lower loss levels.

This study examines the long-term development of Venus's atmosphere, focusing on how composition shifts through interactions between the external atmosphere and internal planetary processes. Although Venus's atmospheric history and formation remain poorly understood, our working hypothesis attributes its evolution primarily to volcanic outgassing influenced by photochemical effects and radiative-convective dynamics. This paper investigates the intricate chemical interactions within an inflating atmosphere, utilizing extensive chemical models to trace various chemical scenarios. We analyze how extensive degassing, moderated by internal and external factors, influences atmospheric chemistry, specifically exploring whether extensive reactions in the lower to middle atmospheric layers deplete active gases like sulfur dioxide ($SO_2$) and carbon monoxide ($CO$) to levels below those expected from pure volcanic emissions. We further assess whether such environmental depletion offers an alternative explanation for Venus atmospheric observations, particularly regarding current data on $CO$ and $SO_2$, which include the Venus Express/VIRTIS/CO spectra and Venus Express/VIRTIS/SO$_2$ data. Additionally, we integrate these findings with existing knowledge of Venus atmospheric history and synthesis from volcanic degassing, especially concerning $CO$ and $SO_2$. The study has significant implications for our understanding of Venus atmospheric evolution and internal structure, with implications extending to other inner planetary atmospheres, such as Mars.

Multivariate point processes are extensively used to analyze events characterized by type, such as neural firing patterns, financial dealings, digital communications, or ecological disasters. Among these, the Hawkes process stands as a prominent model where an event likelihood relies on the process's history; specifically, the focus of this study is on the nonlinear variant, which accounts for excitation and inhibition dynamics across different process dimensions. Within a nonparametric Bayesian framework, we develop a novel implementation of these processes utilizing Gaussian process (GP) priors for the kernel functions defining the impact of past events of each type on the current intensity regarding any type. Although the resulting posterior distribution over Bayesian parameters is inherently infinite-dimensional, we demonstrate that an efficient approximate Bayesian computation can be achieved using only a finite number of cumulative intensity basis functions. This method extends readily to handle additional structural assumptions, such as parametric forms or specific behaviors like self-exciting loops or long memory. Finally, we evaluate the approach through both simulated data and a real-world analysis of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

Conventional solid-state optical materials struggle to meet the demands of next-generation high-power laser systems due to thermal and structural limitations. Plasma-based alternatives present a viable solution, as their optically transparent region extends the full infrared spectrum; however, the broad dispersion range poses a challenge for creating devices that are both simple and efficient. By engineering a spatially varying magnetic field, we induced a plasma with an electron density gradient, which served as a linear polarization waveplate. Leveraging this principle, we constructed a two-layer waveplate interface that successfully switched linear polarization into circular polarization across the 1030-nm wavelength, covering a 30-by-30-millimeter area. This transformation achieved an power efficiency exceeding 93%, a result we validated both through precise numerical simulations and experimental measurements.

Building upon \cite{Ferrara:1971vh, Ferrara:1973vz}, we derive an integral representation for OPE blocks associated with spinning primaries in two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT$_2$). When OPE blocks are constructed from conserved spinning primaries, the integral decomposes into a pair of weighted AdS$_2$ field copies that are smeared along geodesics. Consequently, instead of interpreting consistent currents as geodesic operators in AdS$_3$, conserved current OPE blocks in CFT$_2}$ can alternatively be described via AdS$_2}$ geodesic operators. We further clarify the connection between this formulation and AdS$_3$ massless higher spin fields through HKLL bulk reconstruction \cite{HKLL}, enabling the derivation of closed four-spinning conformal blocks as a factorization of two AdS$_2}$ Geodesic Witten diagrams.

We propose a future generation of lobster-eye optics that utilizes multiplexing to create an even more compact and robust design for X-ray warning systems with extensive viewing fields. This approach substitutes the conventional monolayer of lenses with two stratified layers of elements, each oriented to provide separate narrow fields of view that correspond to distinct sky positions. By eliminating the need for a massive, single monolayer structure, the risk of mechanical deformation leading to performance degradation is significantly reduced. Through ray-tracing simulations, we verify the concept using a two-layer configuration that covers a total viewing field (3σ) of 30 degrees; this setup offers a benefit where the incorporation of multiplexed layers effectively expands the covered field of view by approximately a factor of two compared to a single layer. Given its anticipated smaller footprint and high reliability, this multiplexed lobster-eye technology is ideally suited to enhance the capability of X-ray monitors dedicated to detecting transient events across a wide field of sky.

Building accurate automatic extraction models for visual-heavy documents, such as invoices, is significantly hampered by the expensive collection of thousands of well- annotated training samples required for robust performance. To address this, we present "Selective Labeling," which streamlines the annotation effort by requiring only binary "yes/no" confirmation for candidate extracts flagged by a model initially trained on sparsely labeled data. Merging this approach with a specialized active learning technique to identify instances where the model exhibits the highest uncertainty, we demonstrate via experiments on a real-world invoice extraction task that selective labeling of just 20% to 40% of candidate items—identified by a model trained on densely labeled data—yields a 33% increase in accuracy compared to randomly labeling the same proportion of content.

The LIGO and Virgo collaborations have now been able to detect the complete range of compact binary mergers, which include systems with two black holes (BBH), two neutron stars (BNS), and combinations of neutron stars and black holes (NSBH). Observing both the neutron star components gravitational waves and their accompanying electromagnetic counterparts offers a unique opportunity to constrain fundamental physics. Nevertheless, anticipating these detections relies on robust theoretical modeling. Since many current predictions for NSBH events are based on unconfirmed assumptions, we emphasize the necessity of integrating brown hole formation pathways alongside standard stellar evolution channels into forecasting frameworks. Regarding gravitational wave signatures, we argue that merging black holes with nearly equal masses and spins should exhibit substructure, specifically final spin oscillations or "gongs," distinguishable from the post-merger oscillations seen in BNS collisions. Concerning electromagnetic signatures, we suggest that NSBH events should be categorized into three distinct progenitor families: chemically wind-driven transients, wind-driven magnetized outflows, and accretion-driven transients, with at least one potentially linked to short gamma-ray bursts based on theoretical models of hydrodynamical flow dynamics.

Urban physical contacts and social networking are recognized as key drivers in city economic output, innovation, and public health; however, urban mobility tracking remains a hurdle due to privacy concerns and the high costs of installing sensors on vehicles, at airports, or within homes. This study presents the first comprehensive global contact network constructed from a three-year, four-country satellite dataset covering all urban areas larger than 100 km² from 2016 to 2019. By simulating the transmission of infectious diseases like COVID-19 within these networks, the study identifies that despite the necessity of such contacts for cities to function, their high fragmentation significantly lowers output, suggesting that strict but targeted city-specific lockdown strategies are more effective and economical than nation-wide restrictions.

We have conducted 3D simulations to investigate the formation of high-mass young stellar objects (HMSOs) through the collapse and accretion super-Eddington envelopes surrounding a newly formed protostar. Our study focuses on whether these processes generate super-Eddington accretion bursts and how envelope opacity influences envelope structure and outflow behavior. Our results indicate that such bursts arise from a positive feedback mechanism: increased luminosity thins the envelope, which in turn allows more radiation to exceed the Eddington limit. While our initial models aligned with previously reported observations, subsequent simulations with higher opacity failed to reproduce the typical 100-s timescales characteristic of luminosity spikes; instead, they yielded longer durations that evolved smoothly across the Eddington threshold. Ultimately, we conclude that both initial conditions and opacity values significantly shape envelope dynamics, consistency with existing data currently requires matching low-opacity conditions.

This research investigates the two-dimensional water wave phenomenon characterized by infinite depth, allowing for arbitrary but small amplitude and the presence of uniform shear in the context of extended Kelvin-Bateman (UB) dynamics. In this study, the influence of this shear is examined through the lens of modulational instability affecting Stokes waves. The analysis reveals that the magnitude and orientation of the shear current relative to the wave propagation direction critically influence this instability, a relationship quantified by the Weber number. The discussion also addresses the necessity of nonlinear effects to ensure the conservation of wave energy within the framework of piecewise analytic solutions. By employing a perturbation method at third order, the work derives a non-linear Schrödinger equation with specific coefficients tailored to these UB conditions. The resulting model is validated against existing literature, demonstrating its effectiveness in describing a wide variety of flow scenarios.

Naviging complex, dynamic indoor environments remains a significant challenge for autonomous mobile robots, particularly when deteriorating environmental conditions cause standard sensors to underperform and compromise safe operation. This study introduces a new sonar-based obstacle detection method designed to maintain reliable performance across both pristine and degraded sensor conditions by integrating two distinct nonlinear models. The approach first employs a nonlinear auto-regressive exogenous (NARX) network to learn the non-stationary probability density functions of free and occupied cells directly from sonar data. Building on this foundation, the proposed NARX-based probabilistic (NPP) data fusion combines these outputs with those derived from an occupied cell estimation algorithm known as Gaussian free space (GFS). Evaluations conducted in simulated and real-world environments demonstrate the method's superior accuracy and consistency in generating robust, symmetric, and symmetrically symmetric probability maps, maintaining high standards even when sonar performance declines.

Addressing outliers and noise contamination in datasets, $\ell_1$-norm principal component analysis (L1-PCA) has emerged as a key dimension reduction technique, offering robustness that exceeds that of conventional PCA. However, solving the convex optimization formulation for L1-PCA typically involves a large optimization scale, hindering its application to massive datasets. This paper introduces a scalable and distributed optimization approach tailored for L1-PCA. Our method iteratively alternates between updating small-scale subproblems and employing an efficient coupling mechanism to distribute the global optimization state across nodes in a network. We validate our proposed framework using the MNIST image dataset and an industrial image security clipboard (ISC) robustness classification model, demonstrating both its effectiveness and computational efficiency.

Annotated data are conventionally utilized to input supervised machine learning (ML) models; however, existing pretrained ML models in natural language processing (NLP) inherently possess linguistic features beneficial to streamlining data annotation. We employ the BERT neural language model to facilitate the annotation process within the Emotion Twenty Questions (EMO20Q)—a query-heavy dialogue game focused on character creation—specifically concerning the semantic labelling of communication actions. We begin with a background overview of BERT, the EMO20Q dataset, and assisted annotation workflows, followed by a detailed description of the methods used to fine-tune BERT, specifically optimizing it to verify the accuracy and consistency of already annotated labels. Using paraphrase verification, we classify all textual submissions sharing the same label, evaluating whether each instance qualifies as a paraphrase relative to others. We demonstrate this method serves as a robust strategy for refining textual datasets containing complicated, utterance-specific semantic labels.

Autonomous navigation within unfamiliar environments is crucial for mobile robots, requiring that maps serve as the foundational element. While most existing representations depend on global metric maps supported by error-free state estimation, maintaining drift-free operation and ensuring rapid global consistency proves difficult in expansive, real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce a new mapping architecture called HiTMap designed to outperform traditional approaches. Our solution replaces global metric maps with a hierarchical topology built on submaps, thereby restricting the data maintained to a local metric area necessary for obstacle detection. This shift confines the challenge of global consistency to the map structure itself rather than the sensor data, a task we resolve using our proposed path planner. To validate this framework, we deployed it on both simulated and physical platforms to confirm its efficacy. Additionally, we extend the framework to accommodate various sensors and diverse, complex environments, demonstrating its adaptability.

Precise magnetic field measurements at low sensitivity represent an unresolved challenge in metrology. This paper examines two approaches for performing field-independent measurements using superconductors: the Meissner effect and flux exclusion. In the classic Meissner scenario, an evolving superconductor expels its interior magnetic flux, generating significant fields that demand careful measurement. Conversely, in a type-II superconductor above its lower critical field ($B_c$), flux exclusion occurs; here, the magnetic field is expelled from the material's core because the energy cost of forming normal regions exceeds that of screening currents. This flux exclusion generates fields that must be measured with high precision. The Helium Inductively Coupled Plasma (HICP) source described in this study features a planar design known for its compact dimensions and uniform plasma distribution. A key advantage of this source is the ability to access the helicon discharge mode, a characteristic that allows significant ionization at lower radio frequency (RF) powers compared to other modes. In this work, we examine the relationships between plasma characteristics and various operating parameters, including RF power, grounding configuration, and magnetic field configuration. By altering the grounding scheme and magnetic loop, the study successfully transitioned from the sheath mode to the helicon mode. In both distinct discharge regimes, ion saturation currents were measured to evaluate plasma electron density across different heating scenarios. Rhodamine and Rayex optical fluoresence techniques were also employed to map electron density and temperature, respectively, with results indicating substantial improvements in both metrics when switching from sheath to helicon modes. Finally, based on the experimental data for electron temperature and density, Debye lengths were calculated and used to assess the validity of the Maxwellian assumptions underlying the measured ion saturation current data.

Although automatic nucleus segmentation supports pathologists in diagnosing cancer, most robust models remain impractical for clinical use due to their size and slow inference speeds. By first accurately rough segmenting nuclei and then refining the output with pairwise mask labels to correct errors, NuSAC achieves competitive performance on the CAMELON dataset, matching results from state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, it delivers significantly more compact models and faster inference speeds without a drop in accuracy, ensuring practical clinical applicability.

ViDaExpert serves as a specialized utility for the visualization and analysis of multidimensional vectorial datasets.
